fields.name: Name
fields.evidence: Replication serializer bg3.exe+0x8E10A0 / bg3.exe+0x8E0FB0: dirty bit 1 -> ecs::sync::Serialize(writer, (FixedString *)(DAT_1462805f8 + base)) = offset 0. Toolkit esv::GameTimerSystem::ProcessCreateRequests (EoCServer.dll+0x4197D0) copies the timer request's FixedString name here (the one logged as "Timer: %s" / "Creating timer (%s, %s)") and marks dirty bit 0. Live: an FS index (0x0DD001F0).

fields.name: field_4
fields.evidence: Serializer: dirty bit 2 -> Serialize((FixedString *)(base + 4)). ProcessCreateRequests copies the request's second FixedString (request +0x1C, passed after name, entity, time and flags) here. Live: an FS index (0x25C000A1). Meaning not established (event / owner name?).

fields.name: Elapsed
fields.evidence: Serializer: dirty bit 4 -> ScratchBuffer::Write(base + 8, 4 bytes). Toolkit esv::GameTimerSystem::ProcessTimerUpdates copies esv::GameTimerComponent +0x10 here (dirty index 2); that GameTimer field accumulates frame time and is compared with the duration (+0x14). Live: 0.

fields.name: Duration
fields.evidence: Serializer: dirty bit 8 -> ScratchBuffer::Write(base + 0xC, 4 bytes). ProcessCreateRequests copies the request's +0x10 here (dirty index 3); the same value goes to esv::GameTimerComponent +0x14, the limit the elapsed time is compared with in ProcessTimerUpdates. Live: 90.0 (float).

open_questions: Offsets/widths are from the replication serializer (high); names are inferred from the Toolkit's esv::GameTimerSystem (offsets there come from the Toolkit build).
Only the subset of timers with flag 0x20 in the request mirror into this component (ProcessCreateRequests checks request byte +0x18 & 0x20).
